answer_quotes: Erm, I was always interested in Maths and Physics and I did my – how theoretical physics was – so I started looking into engineering (OK) see if that was suited better.

Erm, I’ve always been very practical. I mean I can guild numbers – anything with key words, or trying to fill up 2 sides of A4 when it only needs half a side, to be precise (Mm) I’ve just never been able to do. And it’s the same kind of thing – both of my parents are the same way
I didn’t want to specify – as much to do – just aero or auto. And, er, mechanical was just – it was varied enough for you to get as much out of it as you wanted to
Er my Dad was, my mum wasn’t.
She thought I should be doing Maths or Accounting, because she thought there was better job prospects and the course wouldn’t be as heavy, so I’d find it easier.
they backed me up a lot for it … the Careers people were really into it, my Physics teacher was really excited about it and things like that.

I expected the course to be more intense than it was, kind of, because it’s always been built up as this really hard course which nobody wants to do … But, it’s what I thought, but it’s not as time consuming as I thought
the worst thing is the group projects possibly, because we don’t get enough information to do a lot of the stuff, so we’re always getting cross
The best bit is I’m finally understanding a lot of stuff … its all starting coming together and we’re looking at more interesting things rather than basic examples.
there’s been a general consensus on our course that the one female lecturer we’ve had is possible the worst role model we could’ve ever asked for and we prefer – we much prefer just having whoever.

Not really mixed groups tend to be the best … if you’ve got a mixed group, usually you can get some back up for everything you’re going to say.

I’ve always wanted to do things like placement stuff, even if it was just to see which bits of engineering I didn’t want to do. … Gain the experience and just seeing how it does work in the real world

I don’t like the idea of it being put through – that these are [university] students … I’d rather have sent in my CV, covering letter or do the on-line thing, and just say, this is me, this is what I’ve done, do you want to employ me or not?
it shows that you have got some idea of erm being grounded in industry rather than saying I know all this theory like everyone else does. You can apply it
the best thing will be meeting – making new contacts … The worst is probably moving to wherever the placement is and being somewhere completely new and having to live with total strangers
Erm, mostly. I’m still a bit worried about not knowing enough, especially because I don’t know exactly where I’m going or what I’ll be expected to do at that company.
anything which sounds like it could be more than just being sat at an office doing one thing time and time again
I’m most interested in looking at things which look at research rather than design work, or where I can go out on site for a bit and come back

my ideal would be working for someone like [company] on [place] because they have the funding, with being linked to the MoD … you’d still have the main defence work which has a huge amount of innovation

I would prefer to stay with research but a lot of people I’ve talked to in companies … you can get almost straight into managerial positions if you want to but I personally find – hold off doing that until I’ve had at least 2/3 years working almost at ground level
hopefully, I’ll have just finished the graduate development programme – somewhere – and be looking at erm getting myself in whatever area I’ve found useful
Hopefully I will have got my chartership (yeah) and still working for the same company – possibly.
